Stability Landscape Across a Stability Measure

Source: R/stability_landscape.R
landscape_surface.Rd

landscape_surface() traces the cups of stability_landscape() over a second axis, a per-sequence stability measure from sequence_metrics() such as self-loop tendency or longitudinal entropy, and returns the cup depth of every state at each point of that axis. At each of n_grid values of the measure, sequences are weighted by a tricube kernel on their distance to that value over the k nearest (Cleveland 1979), and each state's cup depth, \(-\log(1 - P_{ii})\) (the log of its expected stay), is computed from their weighted pooled transitions. With the default measure, longitudinal entropy, moving up the axis goes from the most stable to the most volatile sequences; for a measure where higher means more stable (self-loop tendency, spell durations, initial-state persistence, dominant-state share) it goes the other way. Several measures give one surface each, and a grouped network one set per group.

The measures are computed from the same sequences as the depths, so the cups of the most stable sequences are deep by construction (self-loop tendency in particular is closely tied to the stay probabilities). What the surface adds is which cup deepens as stability rises. A slice's effective_n (\((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\)) shows how many sequences it rests on, and a warning of class nestimate_thin_slice flags slices resting on fewer than five. For change over the programme rather than across sequences, use landscape_trend().

Usage

landscape_surface(
  x,
  measure = "longitudinal_entropy",
  states = NULL,
  k = 30L,
  n_grid = 25L,
  cols = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
summary(object, ends = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
print(x, digits = 2, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_landscape_surface'
plot(x, max_stay = 50, theta = 10, phi = 30, ncol = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

The network or sequences: a transition network from build_network() with method "relative" or "frequency" (or a bare cograph_network of one), a grouped one (netobject_group), a tna model, or a wide sequence data frame or matrix. A network must carry its sequences; a network of another method (for example "glasso") raises an error of class nestimate_not_markov. For the print() and plot() methods: a net_landscape_surface object.

measure

The per-sequence measures to trace, one surface each: one or more numeric columns of sequence_metrics(). Default "longitudinal_entropy". A name that is not a numeric column, or a measure that is the same for every sequence, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

states

Every state, each named once, in drawing order. Default NULL, the alphabetical order. A vector that leaves out, adds or repeats a state raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

k

The number of nearest sequences each slice is weighted over, at least 5. Default 30, capped at the number of usable sequences.

n_grid

The number of slices, at least 2, spread evenly between the 5th and 95th percentile of the measure. If these percentiles coincide for a measure that is not constant, its full range is used. Default 25.

cols

For a wide data frame: the columns holding the positions. Needed when they are not a numbered run (T1, T2, ...) or one of them is called action; such a frame without cols raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. Default NULL.

object

For the summary() method: a net_landscape_surface object.

ends

For the summary() method: TRUE (default) compares the low and the high end of each measure; FALSE returns every slice.

...

Ignored.

digits

For the print() method: decimal places. Default 2.

max_stay

For the plot() method: the longest expected stay drawn, in steps, a number above 1. Cups of states whose expected stay is longer (including states never left in a slice) are drawn at the depth log(max_stay), a display floor only. Default 50.

theta, phi

For the plot() method: the viewing angles passed to graphics::persp(). Defaults 10 and 30.

ncol

For the plot() method: panels per row. Default NULL, one column per measure and one row per network.

Value

A net_landscape_surface object. print() shows each state's depth at the low and the high end of each measure and the range of effective sequences per slice; summary() returns the tables below; plot() draws one graphics::persp() surface per network and measure on a shared depth scale, the most stable end of each measure in front (for a measure with no stability direction, the low end) and the surface shaded from green (deep) to orange (shallow). print() and plot() return their input invisibly.

summary() returns a data frame. With ends = TRUE: one row per network, measure and state, with group, measure, state, low_value, depth_at_low, high_value and depth_at_high. With ends = FALSE: one row per network, measure, slice and state, with group, measure, value, state, depth, dwell and effective_n.

The object's fields:

slices

Every slice, as summary(x, ends = FALSE) returns it.

states

The states, in drawing order.

measure, groups

The measures traced and the network names ("network" for a single one).

k

The number of nearest sequences per slice.

Details

Network input replays the network's per-sequence weighting, concatenation and boundary markers; concatenated sequences are weighted as one unit. Scaled, thresholded or otherwise modified networks whose weights do not match their stored sequences are refused; pass the original sequences to estimate a new landscape.

Sequences with fewer than two observed positions, or no value of the measure, are left out. The kernel's half-width is the distance to the k-th nearest sequence, but at least 1/50 of the measure's range. A state that does not occur in a slice has an NA depth and leaves a gap in the surface, and one that is never left in a slice has an infinite depth.

Errors

nestimate_not_markov for a network that is not a transition network; nestimate_bad_input for an unknown, non-numeric or constant measure, bad states, input without sequences, or a network whose weights cannot be rebuilt from its sequences (a scaled or thresholded one included); nestimate_landscape_unestimable for fewer than five usable sequences. Warning nestimate_thin_slice when slices rest on fewer than five effective sequences.

References

Cleveland, W. S. (1979). Robust locally weighted regression and smoothing scatterplots. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 74, 829–836.

Kramers, H. A. (1940). Brownian motion in a field of force and the diffusion model of chemical reactions. Physica, 7, 284–304.

See also

stability_landscape, sequence_metrics

Examples

net <- build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
surf <- landscape_surface(net, measure = "longitudinal_entropy",
  states = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"))
surf
#> Landscape surface: 3 states, 1 network x 1 measure, 30 nearest sequences per slice
#> 
#> Cup depth (log of the expected stay) at the low and the high end of each measure:
#>               measure      state  low depth_at_low high depth_at_high
#>  longitudinal_entropy Disengaged 0.11         1.95 0.96          0.57
#>  longitudinal_entropy    Average 0.11         1.42 0.96          0.57
#>  longitudinal_entropy     Active 0.11         3.03 0.96          0.54
#> 
#> Effective sequences per slice: network 13.3-25.7
# \donttest{
plot(surf)

# }
